findings.claim: The diff adds a provider_pool field to OrchestrationConfig and routes it into the review path, which now calls ProviderPoolManager.detect_exhaustion, directly contradicting the still-present module comment a few lines above stating 'the orchestrator holds no provider pool, and wiring one in would duplicate an abstraction that already exists one layer up.'
findings.evidence: Lines 54-57 of orchestrator.py (unmodified by this diff) explain that provider-pool awareness is deliberately kept out of the orchestrator and left to the caller. The new `provider_pool: Optional[Any] = None` field is threaded into `ReviewRunner.execute_review_cycle(..., provider_pool=self.config.provider_pool)`, and that code path (review_runner.py `invoke_reviewer_with_failover`) calls `provider_pool.detect_exhaustion(candidate, agent_res)` directly -- the orchestrator now does hold and exercise a provider pool for the review step, while the implementation step still leaves exhaustion classification to the caller (marathon.py). The design-boundary comment was not updated to reflect this new asymmetry, so it now misdescribes the actual architecture.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the comment block at orchestrator.py:52-57 to describe the new split explicitly (implementation-exhaustion classification stays with the caller; review-exhaustion/failover is now orchestrator-owned via `provider_pool`), or, if the asymmetry is unintentional, keep review-side failover decisions with the caller too, to preserve the original single clean boundary.

findings.claim: Sharing self.provider_pool between marathon's implementation-failover loop and the orchestrator's review step means a review-side provider exhaustion (newly possible because of this diff) is recorded into the pool but is invisible to the loop's own failover decision, which can cause the governed-fix attempt to abort without retrying a different provider -- the opposite of the intent stated in the added comment ('review-time quota exhaustion is visible to implementation failover').
findings.evidence: marathon.py:1423 computes `event = self.provider_pool.detect_exhaustion(provider, exec_res, ...)` using only `exec_res = result.provider_execution` (the implementer's result). If implementation succeeds but every review candidate then gets exhausted inside `execute_review_cycle` (via the newly-wired provider_pool), `has_failure=True` forces `requires_remediation=True` (review_runner.py:588), so `orchestrator.run()` either burns remediation cycles against findings that don't exist or ends with a final_state other than 'complete'. Back in marathon.py, since `event is None` (line 1444), the loop takes the 'do not fail over' branch and returns False immediately (line 1444-1448) instead of selecting `next_candidates` and retrying with an alternate provider, even though the shared pool now genuinely has exhaustion information from the review attempt.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold review-side exhaustion (e.g. surfaced from `cycle_res.reviewer_results[*].attempts` or a dedicated signal returned by execute_review_cycle) into the `event`/failover decision in marathon.py's retry loop, so a fully-exhausted reviewer pool triggers the same next_candidates retry path as an exhausted implementer, instead of falling through to remediation cycles or an immediate failure.
